issues.description: Bedrock client created per LLMContextFrame causes connection churn and credential staleness
issues.detail: process_frame opens a fresh `aioboto3.Session().client('bedrock-agentcore', ...)` on every incoming context frame. For a streaming voice pipeline this means repeated TLS handshakes and credential resolution per turn. The client should be created once (e.g., in start/setup) and reused, or cached at minimum.

issues.description: Unhandled JSON / network exceptions will propagate and break the pipeline
issues.detail: `default_response_to_output_transformer` calls `json.loads(response_line)` with no try/except, and `invoke_agent_runtime` and the async iteration over `response['response']` are unguarded. Any malformed event or transient AWS error will raise inside `process_frame`, crashing the processor. Wrap with try/except and log/push an error frame.

issues.description: Public parameter `agentArn` violates PEP 8 and Python conventions used elsewhere in pipecat
issues.detail: The constructor exposes `agentArn` (camelCase) as a public kwarg while every other parameter uses snake_case (`aws_access_key`, etc.). This is a public API surface; once shipped it is painful to rename. Use `agent_arn` and keep camelCase only at the AWS API boundary.

issues.description: Timeout-based end-of-response detection can fire mid-stream and produce wrong bookends
issues.detail: `_close_output_response_after_timeout` sleeps 1s and emits `LLMFullResponseEndFrame`. If the agent stream has a >1s gap between chunks, End is pushed prematurely, then the next chunk re-opens a new response — splitting one logical turn into multiple. Since the stream end is known when the async-for exits, the explicit close at the bottom is enough; the timer is dangerous.

issues.description: Naive `data: ` SSE parsing drops multi-line data and ignores other event fields
issues.detail: The parser splits on `\n` and slices `line[6:]`, but real SSE allows multi-line `data:` values concatenated by the client, comment lines starting with `:`, and event/id fields. Lines that don't start with `data: ` (e.g., `event: ...`) currently log a warning every time, which will be noisy and may indicate dropped content.

issues.description: Default transformer skips assistant messages and silently no-ops on tool/specific messages
issues.detail: `default_context_to_payload_transformer` only accepts the last message if its role is `user` or `system`. If the last message is `assistant` (common after tool calls or follow-up) or an `LLMSpecificMessage`, the processor returns silently with no log, making misconfiguration hard to diagnose. At least log a debug message explaining why no payload was sent.

review.summary: New AWS Bedrock AgentCore processor is straightforward but has several pre-merge concerns. The most important are a per-frame client construction pattern, unguarded JSON/AWS exceptions that will crash the pipeline, and a timeout-based response-end heuristic that can split a single agent turn. Public API naming uses camelCase (`agentArn`) inconsistent with the rest of pipecat, and SSE parsing is fragile. No tests are added for the new module.
